accepted_scope: Reduced-order heated-flow solver/reduction consistency benchmark against the public NASA Wind-US computational reference, with public Burrows-Kurkov experimental profiles retained as independent qualitative/contextual evidence only.

grid_convergence.acceptance_gate: Absolute conservative-target errors < 2% and 160-to-320 refinement changes < 0.5% for Mach, static pressure, and static temperature.

thermodynamic_sensitivity.interpretation: The substantial output shift under lower gamma confirms that the benchmark claim is conditional on the frozen calorically-perfect effective-gas reduction. It must not be generalized to finite-rate chemistry or variable-composition thermodynamics.

experimental_context.reason: The public experiment supplies nonuniform exit probe profiles whereas the present solver produces a single cross-sectionally reduced state. Unsupported averaging or profile fitting would create a misleading experimental-validation claim.
experimental_context.permitted_statement: The public Burrows-Kurkov profiles remain independent context demonstrating the strongly nonuniform reacting exit field; they are not used to construct the computational-reference-derived inlet, energy source, momentum source, or conservative exit target.

claim_boundaries: Accepted: numerical/reduction consistency of the quasi-one-dimensional heated-flow model under NASA-reference-derived signed energy and momentum closures.
Accepted: reproducible public-data provenance, conservative inlet/exit moment matching, grid convergence, and gamma sensitivity reporting.
Not accepted: independent experimental validation of a one-dimensional bulk Mach or temperature scalar.
Not accepted: finite-rate chemistry validation, H2/H2O species validation, measured chemical heat-release reconstruction, or wall-friction identification.
Not accepted: LBW/YBW classification. P11.3 requires a separate authoritative mode definition and observable/threshold evidence.

next_stage.scope: Research and freeze authoritative LBW/YBW definitions, observables, thresholds, applicability limits, and uncertainty before any regime classifier or map is promoted.
